2.title: The exam, definitively
2.text: The authoritative statement of the format, from the lecturer's own exam session. Written, in English. 60 minutes, split 30 minutes international law and 30 minutes EU law. Maximum 60 points, 30 from each half. To pass: at least 30 points overall AND at least 15 points in each half. Offered four times a year — the dates listed are January, March/April, June and October 2026, always to be checked against the SSC website. Register and de-register in time, and address any problem to the SSC, not to the professors.

cards.q: How is the StEOP exam structured in time and points?
cards.a: 60 minutes: 30 for international law, 30 for EU law. 60 points maximum, 30 per half. Pass at 30 points overall with a minimum of 15 in each half.

3.title: What the lecture can and cannot do
3.text: The aim of the class is to illustrate the dynamics and system of EU law within selected areas — not to list things but to get the audience thinking and, ideally, understanding. Two consequences the lecturer draws: not everything can be covered, so you must READ; and the lecture format means you must PRACTISE.

4.title: What the EU half asks
4.text: Two components. Problem questions mainly on FORMAL EU law, but also on the basics of internal market and competition law in the way they interact with formal EU law. And one CASE EXERCISE with open questions and less guidance on formal EU law — with the warning repeated in bold: without solving at least part of the case you cannot pass. Hence: practise case exercises.

cards.q: What are the two components of the EU half of the exam, and which is decisive?
cards.a: Problem questions on formal EU law (plus internal market and competition basics as they interact with it), and one open case exercise. The case is decisive: without solving at least part of it the exam cannot be passed.

5.title: The lecturer's study advice
5.text: Her own list: use videos, books and articles, practice and discussion; practise, practise, practise; attend an exercise; work in a study group; and do the quizzes in the Moodle group. Note what is absent — there is no advice to memorise, and every item on the list is active rather than passive.

7.title: The preparatory exercises
7.text: Four PUE courses, places limited to 45-50 students each; Hornkohl's January course is live-streamed, with a further exercise in March 2026.

8.title: Hornkohl's exercise in detail
8.text: Hypothetical mock cases, online quizzes, discussion of EU law questions and a mock written exam — described by the lecturer as practice, NOT comprehensive coverage. Registered students are graded on two Moodle assignments at 50 per cent each; listeners may attend and receive the mock exam, uncorrected.
